runtime_language: Language-agnostic Symphony service specification plus experimental Elixir/OTP reference implementation. The reference implementation declares Elixir ~> 1.19 and mise pins elixir 1.19.5-otp-28 with erlang 28.
codex_invocation_method: Starts bash -lc <codex.command> in the per-issue workspace; default codex.command is `codex app-server`; communicates with Codex app-server over stdio using JSON-RPC-style messages.
credentials_required: LINEAR_API_KEY or tracker.api_key for Linear-backed operation
Authenticated Codex CLI/app-server environment for real Codex runs
Git/GitHub credentials only if WORKFLOW.md hooks or agent prompt clone private repos, push branches, or open PRs
SSH credentials only if worker.ssh_hosts is configured
safety_controls_found: Per-issue workspace directories under configured workspace.root
Workspace root containment and symlink escape checks before local Codex launch
Codex cwd set to the per-issue workspace, not the source repo
Default Codex approval policy rejects sandbox/rules/MCP approval requests when omitted
Default Codex thread sandbox is workspace-write
Default Codex turn sandbox policy is rooted at the issue workspace and sets networkAccess false
CLI requires explicit --i-understand-that-this-will-be-running-without-the-usual-guardrails acknowledgement before starting
Hook timeout configuration with default 60000 ms
Codex turn timeout, read timeout, and stall timeout settings
Stall detection restarts inactive sessions with backoff
Unsupported dynamic tool calls return structured failure instead of stalling
Optional dashboard/API binds to loopback by default
major_blockers: Official reference implementation is Linear-first; no GitHub Issues adapter is shipped.
No durable file-based queue adapter is shipped; the memory tracker is in-memory and test/local-development oriented.
Reference implementation adds an Elixir/Erlang/BEAM runtime stack to AI-Orchestrator.
Useful real runs require authenticated Codex app-server and generally network access to OpenAI services.
The provided example WORKFLOW.md is high-trust and sets approval_policy: never.
WORKFLOW.md hooks are arbitrary shell scripts and must be treated as trusted executable configuration.
The CLI starts a long-running polling service, so any dry run must explicitly prevent real dispatch or use a fake/no-op tracker and fake/no-op Codex command.
commands_run: rg -n "github|GitHub|file-based|file based|filesystem|memory|tracker.kind|WORKFLOW|app-server|Codex|Linear|stall|approval_policy|networkAccess|danger|guardrails|without any guardrails" README.md SPEC.md elixir
